rationale: Features: every catalogue column that is neither an identifier (claim_id, member_id, rendering_npi excluded) nor label-derived (fraud_pattern_type excluded; manifest shows it null in 12,198 of 12,845 rows, consistent with being populated only when fraud_label = 1, so it would leak the target). The 17 retained columns are claim attributes available at prediction time, so id_fields_present and label_derived_present should both be empty in feature_list.json. Split: test_size 0.25 holds out a quarter of claims; stratify true preserves the ~5% positive prevalence in both partitions, with the run seed and prevalence_train/prevalence_test recorded per the split output. Preprocessing: fit_on train_only so the one-hot encoder and scaler never see held-out rows; standard scaling because logistic regression is sensitive to the amount and units columns' scale. Models: logistic_regression plus one tree-based model (random_forest) as the task requires; class_weight balanced because the label is heavily imbalanced and metrics are reported at a fixed 0.5 threshold, so unweighted models would default to near-zero recall. Report: the four caveats map to the task's stated limitations (synthetic label, class imbalance, baseline model, no operational use); show_denominators prints prevalence and confusion-matrix rates with their denominators; cite_artifacts ties every results bullet to model_metrics.json, metrics.json or a saved figure.
